objective: Complete the requirements correctly with minimum whole-task elapsed time and total operational cost, including coordination, verification and recovery. Input size is secondary.

initial_count.instructions: Select the candidate task count that best completes the goal. Consider dependencies, workload, prior failures, worker capabilities and total verification/recovery overhead.

ready_selection.instructions: Select which dependency-ready task batch to execute next. Consider critical dependencies, available concurrency, carried evidence and whole-task completion time. Every option is executable; preserve ownership.

post_worker_review.instructions: Review the worker result against the assigned requirements, observed checks and full carried evidence. Accept only if no known substantive gap remains. Choose repair for a concrete remaining gap. Do not claim independent benchmark success.

failure_recovery.instructions: Choose whether one bounded repair by the same scoped worker can address this confirmed failure using available evidence, or stop this task. Never retry an uncertain provider outcome. Prefer whole-task correctness and completion efficiency.

fixed_profile: Worker model and effort are fixed for the paired experiment; bypass model/profile selection and record this restriction.
completion: All selected tasks accepted and whole verification callback passes yields ready_for_independent_grade, never benchmark success.

callback_contract.execute: ({task,plan,brief,evidence,attempt,repair,model,effort}) => result; throw {uncertain:true} or {outcome_uncertain:true} for uncertain outcomes, which are never retried
callback_contract.verify: ({scope:'task'|'whole',task?,plan,brief,evidence,workerResult?}) => {ok:boolean,...observations}; must mechanically check owned required files for task scope
callback_contract.record: (event) => void or Promise; events have monotonic sequence and complete revisioned evidence snapshots on decision requests
